For swept distance along the river \(x\) to be minimum, let angle \(\theta\) between \(u\) and \(v\) be \(\cfrac{\pi}{2}+\theta\) as shown in figure.

Then, time required to cross the river \(t=\cfrac{d}{v\cos\theta}\)

Swept distance \(x=(u-v\sin\theta)\times t=(u-v\sin\theta)\times\cfrac{d}{v\cos\theta}\)

For x to be minimum, \(\cfrac{dx}{d\theta}=0\)

\(\Rightarrow \cfrac{ud\sin\theta}{\cos^{2}\theta}-d\sec^{2}\theta =0\)

\(\Rightarrow u\sin\theta - v =0\)

\(\theta=\sin^{-1}\left(\cfrac{v}{u}\right)\)

\(\therefore x\) is minimum at angle \(\theta = \cfrac{\pi}{2}+\sin^{-1}\left(\cfrac{v}{u}\right)\)

Hence, both statements are correct.
